findings.title: Possible association disruption: conflicting AP responses
findings.detail: 2 connection attempts by 96:33:36:9d:5b:d8 to AP 30:86:2d:c0:07:c0 received an unprotected disconnect and then a successful association response from the same claimed AP. This inconsistent state can indicate spoofed pre-key disconnects, including on PMF-required networks
evidence: association request frame 632, unprotected disconnect frame 634 (reason 6), followed by successful association response within 1 s
association request frame 995, unprotected disconnect frame 997 (reason 6), followed by successful association response within 1 s
findings.benign_explanation: capture reordering, stale retransmissions, or an AP firmware/state mismatch may also produce conflicting responses; this is a suspected disruption, not proof

findings.title: Unprotected deauth on an MFP-required network
findings.detail: "WPA3" (30:86:2d:c0:07:c0) requires management frame protection. Established protected associations should reject forged unprotected disconnects, but frames sent before key installation can still disrupt connection setup; this capture alone does not establish whether the frames were effective
